title: marimo
name: marimo
description: Python notebooks saved as plain .py files, where running a cell reruns everything that depends on it, with SQL cells, interactive widgets and a dataframe explorer built in. pandas, Polars, DuckDB and Altair come installed. Source: https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo

env.name: MARIMO_PASSWORD
env.label: Password (required)
env.description: What you'll log in with. Anything long and hard to guess, or generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16

env.name: MARIMO_SESSION_SECRET
env.label: Session secret
env.description: Keeps you logged in across restarts and updates. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Left blank, every restart logs you out.

env.name: MARIMO_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without one. Then open http://<your-host>:2718 (or whichever port you picked) and log in with it. The home page lists every notebook in the marimo-notebooks volume, marimo's tutorials included, and new ones save there as plain .py files. Your settings live in marimo-home. Packages you add from inside a notebook go into the container rather than a volume, so they're gone after an update and you'll need to install them again. Whoever logs in can run any Python on the server, so keep it off the open internet unless it's behind HTTPS. Docs: docs.marimo.io
